title: "Materials"
jupyter: python3
fig-align: center
---

MolecularNodes ships a small set of pre-built materials, available as classes in
`mn.material`. Instantiating one creates a new, independent Blender material —
starting values are set through the constructor, and every parameter remains
tweakable on the instance afterwards.

```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn
from molecularnodes.nodes import geometry as g
from nodebpy import shader as s

cv = mn.Canvas(engine="EEVEE", resolution=(800, 800), transparent=True)
```

## Pre-built materials

Pass a preset directly to `add_style()`. The parameters map onto the inputs of
the nodes inside the material, so changing them updates the render immediately.

```{python}
# | label: fig-material-preset
# | fig-cap: The Ambient Occlusion material is performant and aesthetically pleasing. Parameters can be tweaked on the instance after creation.
# | layout-ncol: 2
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "distance=2.0"
# |   - "distance=0.15"

mat = mn.material.AmbientOcclusion(distance=2.0)
mol = mn.Molecule.fetch("8H1B").add_style("surface", material=mat)

cv.look_at(mol)
display(cv.snapshot())

mat.distance = 0.15
cv.snapshot()
```

To swap the material on an already-created style, assign a new material to the
style node's material socket:

```{python}
# | label: fig-change-material-flat
# | layout-ncol: 1
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "Flat material with outline"
flat = mn.material.Flat(thickness=0.2)
mol.tree.tree.nodes["Style Surface"].inputs["Material"].default_value = (
    flat.material
)
cv.snapshot()
```

Each preset is a separate material datablock, so tweaking one style's material
never affects another's. The underlying Blender material is always available as
`.material`, and the nodes used to build it are kept as attributes on the
instance (e.g. `mat.ao`, `mat.bsdf`) for access to anything not exposed as a
parameter.

## Custom materials

For full control, build a material from scratch with the
[`nodebpy`](https://bradyajohnston.github.io/nodebpy) shader nodes. Anything
built inside the `with s.material()` block becomes the material's node tree,
and the `MNColor` node provides the per-atom colors.

```{python}
# | label: fig-material-custom
# | fig-cap: A custom material built with nodebpy's shader nodes.

with s.material("Custom Material") as custom:
    custom.nodes.clear()
    col = mn.nodes.shader.MNColor()
    ao = s.AmbientOcclusion(col, distance=1.0, samples=128)
    ao.o.color >> s.MaterialOutput().i.surface

# regular node lookup and property assignment
mol.tree.tree.nodes["Style Surface"].inputs["Material"].default_value = (
    custom.material
)
cv.snapshot()
```

## Render Engines and Materials

The different render engines handle materials diferently.
```{python}
import MDAnalysis as mda
import itertools
from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD

cv = mn.Canvas(resolution=(800, 800), transparent=True)
```


```{python}
# | warning: false
# | label: fig-eevee-raytracing
# | fig-cap: "How different materials behave in each render engine"
# | layout-ncol: 2
# | fig-subcap:
# |   - "Cycles + Default"
# |   - "EEVEE + Default"
# |   - "Cycles + Ambient Occlusion"
# |   - "EEVEE + Ambient Occlusion"
# |   - "Cycles + Flat"
# |   - "EEVEE + Flat"
# |   - "Cycles + Squishy"
# |   - "EEVEE + Squishy"

mol = mn.Molecule.load(PSF, DCD)
with mol.tree.reset() as (atoms, join):
    style = g.StyleSpheres(sphere="Instance")
    style.i["Quality"].default_value = 4
    color = g.ColorElement(c=g.RandomColor(g.ChainID()))
    atoms >> g.SetColor(color=color) >> style >> join

cv.look_at(mol)
engines = [mn.scene.Cycles(samples=32), mn.scene.EEVEE()]
materials = [
    mn.material.Default(),
    mn.material.AmbientOcclusion(),
    mn.material.Flat(),
    mn.material.Squishy(),
]
for mat, eng in itertools.product(materials, engines):
    cv.engine = eng
    style.i.material.default_value = mat.material
    cv.snapshot()
```
